chunk_findings.detail: The bug requires capacity and conformance to be enforced at launch as well as in scoring, and states that launch.py still does not read either. This change only adds `Lane.level` / `Lane.pools` and checks them inside `refusals` when a caller already filled them. Nothing here, and no launch.py edit, sets those fields from a measured conformance run or from live endpoint headroom. A launch of three lanes against an endpoint whose limit is 2 still builds default `Lane`s (`level=0`, `pools=()`); with the default `conformance_min_level` of 0 the new branch does not fire, and `CAPACITY.refusals(())` is never given the full pool, so the oversubscribe still proceeds.

chunk_findings.detail: SW-capacity and SW-conformance are still not read at launch or by the scheduler. `Request.level`/`Request.pools` and `dispatch` `Source.level`/`Source.pools` default to `0` and `()`, and this change never fills them from the conformance store or `capacity.view`. Scoring only refuses whatever the caller already stuffed in. Given an operator setting `conformance_min_level=2` and an endpoint with `busy==limit`, every existing `Request(...)` / source still launches with level 0 and empty pools, so a lane that actually passed conformance is refused as unmeasured while three lanes on a full endpoint are not refused at all (`CAPACITY.refusals(())` sees no pools). The new tests only construct `Lane`/`Source` with the fields already set, so they never catch that.

chunk_findings.detail: `CAPACITY.acquire` is used as a `with` that only covers `drv.start(prep.spec)`. chunk_findings.detail: `Launched` stores `slots` via an `ExitStack`, but the slots context manager is never closed when the lane eventually stops or finishes execution. Because `slots` is left open for the lifetime of the `Launched` object and the caller is expected to manually close it ("close it after the lane stops"), any code path that drops the `Launched` object without explicitly calling `slots.close()` (such as normal process exit, task completion without explicit cleanup, or exceptions during lane monitoring) will leak the acquired capacity slots permanently, causing a resource leak that starves subsequent lanes of capacity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:258

chunk_findings.detail: `CAPACITY.acquire` is entered on an `ExitStack`, but only `TimeoutError` calls `slots.close()` before the exception leaves `launch`. If `drv.start(prep.spec)` raises anything else (for example `RuntimeError` or `OSError`), `enter_context` has already taken the endpoint slots and the local `slots` is discarded as the exception propagates. `ExitStack` does not release on garbage collection, so those slots stay held for the process lifetime. A later launch of the same route then waits out `slot_wait_s` and returns `Refused("endpoint slot: ...")` even though no lane is running. The previous `with` released on every exception; this rewrite does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:230

chunk_findings.detail: On the success path the open `ExitStack` is only stored on the returned `Launched` and never closed. This change does not close it when the lane stops, and `contextlib.ExitStack` has no `__del__` that calls `close()`. After `endpoint_slots` successful launches of one route, every later launch times out even if those lanes have already finished, because nothing in this change releases the pools. Holding the lock only until an unspecified caller remembers to close a new field does not enforce “release the endpoint for the next lane.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:261

chunk_findings.detail: SW-capacity and SW-conformance are still not read at launch or by the scheduler. `Request.level`/`Request.pools` and `dispatch` `Source.level`/`Source.pools` default to `0` and `()`, and this change never fills them from the conformance store or `capacity.view`. Scoring only refuses whatever the caller already stuffed in. Given an operator setting `conformance_min_level=2` and an endpoint with `busy==limit`, every existing `Request(...)` / source still launches with level 0 and empty pools, so a lane that actually passed conformance is refused as unmeasured while three lanes on a full endpoint are not refused at all (`CAPACITY.refusals(())` sees no pools). The new tests only construct `Lane`/`Source` with the fields already set, so they never catch that.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:66

chunk_findings.detail: `CAPACITY.acquire` is used as a `with` that only covers `drv.start(prep.spec)`. Start returns a handle and the function continues (`if isinstance(h, Result)`), so the lane is still running after `__exit__` releases the slots. Two later launches of the same route can both acquire the endpoint after the first `start` returns and oversubscribe it; the comment’s “hold for the lane’s lifetime” is not what this scope does, so B11d484ec15’s capacity enforcement is not actually in effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:221

chunk_findings.detail: `Launched` stores `slots` via an `ExitStack`, but the slots context manager is never closed when the lane eventually stops or finishes execution. Because `slots` is left open for the lifetime of the `Launched` object and the caller is expected to manually close it ("close it after the lane stops"), any code path that drops the `Launched` object without explicitly calling `slots.close()` (such as normal process exit, task completion without explicit cleanup, or exceptions during lane monitoring) will leak the acquired capacity slots permanently, causing a resource leak that starves subsequent lanes of capacity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:258

chunk_findings.detail: `CAPACITY.acquire` is entered on an `ExitStack`, but only `TimeoutError` calls `slots.close()` before the exception leaves `launch`. If `drv.start(prep.spec)` raises anything else (for example `RuntimeError` or `OSError`), `enter_context` has already taken the endpoint slots and the local `slots` is discarded as the exception propagates. `ExitStack` does not release on garbage collection, so those slots stay held for the process lifetime. A later launch of the same route then waits out `slot_wait_s` and returns `Refused("endpoint slot: ...")` even though no lane is running. The previous `with` released on every exception; this rewrite does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:230

chunk_findings.detail: On the success path the open `ExitStack` is only stored on the returned `Launched` and never closed. This change does not close it when the lane stops, and `contextlib.ExitStack` has no `__del__` that calls `close()`. After `endpoint_slots` successful launches of one route, every later launch times out even if those lanes have already finished, because nothing in this change releases the pools. Holding the lock only until an unspecified caller remembers to close a new field does not enforce “release the endpoint for the next lane.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:261

chunk_findings.detail: `Launched.release()` only closes the `ExitStack` if some caller remembers to invoke it, and this change never does. The new comment states that nothing in this module closes the hold and that `ExitStack` does not release on garbage collection. After `endpoint_slots` successful launches of one route, every later `CAPACITY.acquire` waits out `slot_wait` even though those lanes have already stopped, because no stop, monitor, or process-exit path calls `release()`. Adding an unused closer does not enforce SW-capacity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:62

chunk_findings.detail: The new `except BaseException` closes slots and re-raises, but unlike the `TimeoutError` handler and the `isinstance(h, Result)` failure path it does not call `OC.cleanup(req.home)`. If `drv.start(prep.spec)` raises `RuntimeError` after the home was prepared, the slots are freed and the exception propagates with the prepared home left in place, so a retry can collide with that leftover state.

chunk_findings.detail: The bug requires capacity and conformance to be enforced at launch as well as in scoring, and states that launch.py still does not read either. This change only adds `Lane.level` / `Lane.pools` and checks them inside `refusals` when a caller already filled them. Nothing here, and no launch.py edit, sets those fields from a measured conformance run or from live endpoint headroom. A launch of three lanes against an endpoint whose limit is 2 still builds default `Lane`s (`level=0`, `pools=()`); with the default `conformance_min_level` of 0 the new branch does not fire, and `CAPACITY.refusals(())` is never given the full pool, so the oversubscribe still proceeds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/score.py:140

chunk_findings.detail: LaneSource.level and LaneSource.pools still default to 0 and (), and this change never assigns them from the conformance store or a capacity probe — only launch._constraints calls conformance_level/endpoint_pools, and only the new test builds a source with those fields set. A scheduler that constructs LaneSource the way every existing caller does (approved/live/cap only) still gets lane_of → Lane(level=0, pools=()). refusals then sees no pool headroom, so three lanes against an endpoint whose limit is 2 are all admitted; measured conformance is never applied on that path either. Threading optional fields does not enforce SW-capacity or SW-conformance in scoring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/dispatch.py:105

chunk_findings.detail: `launch` now takes endpoint slots into `Launched.slots` and only frees them in `Launched.release()`, and the new comment states the stack is not closed on garbage collection. Nothing in this change calls `release()` (`dispatch.py` is comment-only). Given `endpoint_slots=1`, a successful launch of lane A, then A stopping, the slot stays busy; the next launch waits `slot_wait_s`, raises `TimeoutError`, and returns `Refused("endpoint slot: ...")` even though no lane is running, so capacity enforcement deadlocks the endpoint after the first wave.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/launch.py:271

chunk_findings.detail: The only regression added for B11d484ec15 never calls launch, score, or capacity. `test_conformance_level_expires_after_max_age` only saves a `Report` and asserts `LN.conformance_level` age handling (`max_age_s=30` at `now=1000.0` stays 3, at `now=2000.0` becomes 0). Unfixed `launch.py`/`score.py` that never read capacity or conformance, and three lanes oversubscribing one endpoint, still pass this test, so it cannot fail the bug it is supposed to close. The `max_age_s=0` case also locks in “0 means never expire” rather than an enforcement check.
